# ArchGuard rules reference (spec 2.0.0)

Roles: `DOMAIN`, `APPLICATION`, `INBOUND_PORT`, `OUTBOUND_PORT`, `INBOUND_ADAPTER`, `OUTBOUND_ADAPTER`, `COMPOSITION_ROOT`. Types matching no role are `UNCLASSIFIED`.

## Allowed dependencies by profile

A cell names the rule that forbids a dependency from the row role to the column role; `ok` means allowed. `infrastructure` means framework and persistence APIs listed in `spec/infrastructure/<language>.yml` (for example `jakarta.persistence.`, `org.springframework.`, `sqlalchemy`, `@nestjs/`). Abbreviations: IN_ = INBOUND_, OUT_ = OUTBOUND_, ROOT = COMPOSITION_ROOT.

### `clean`: Clean architecture

Same dependency rule as hexagonal, using the standard role vocabulary (entities = DOMAIN, use cases = APPLICATION plus ports, interface adapters = INBOUND/OUTBOUND_ADAPTER, frameworks and drivers = COMPOSITION_ROOT plus infrastructure). Additionally forbids package cycles inside the analyzed code.

Includes: `hexagonal`.

| from \ to | DOMAIN | APPLICATION | IN_PORT | OUT_PORT | IN_ADAPTER | OUT_ADAPTER | ROOT | infrastructure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DOMAIN** | ok | HEX-001 | ok | ok | HEX-001 | HEX-001 | HEX-001 | HEX-001 |
| **APPLICATION** | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-002 | HEX-002 | HEX-002 | ok |
| **IN_PORT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-003 | HEX-003 | HEX-003 | HEX-003 |
| **OUT_PORT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-003 | HEX-003 | HEX-003 | HEX-003 |
| **IN_ADAPTER** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-004 | ok | ok |
| **OUT_ADAPTER** | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-004 | ok | ok | ok |
| **ROOT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |

Also activates: CYCLE-001.

### `ddd`: Domain-driven design bounded contexts

Declared bounded contexts may only use each other's explicitly exposed packages, and the context dependency graph must be acyclic. Contexts are declared in the policy, never inferred.

Also activates: DDD-001, DDD-002.

### `hexagonal`: Hexagonal (ports and adapters)

The core (DOMAIN, APPLICATION, ports) owns its contracts and never depends on adapters, the composition root or infrastructure APIs. Adapters implement ports and are wired in the composition root. Inbound and outbound adapters do not call each other directly.

| from \ to | DOMAIN | APPLICATION | IN_PORT | OUT_PORT | IN_ADAPTER | OUT_ADAPTER | ROOT | infrastructure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DOMAIN** | ok | HEX-001 | ok | ok | HEX-001 | HEX-001 | HEX-001 | HEX-001 |
| **APPLICATION** | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-002 | HEX-002 | HEX-002 | ok |
| **IN_PORT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-003 | HEX-003 | HEX-003 | HEX-003 |
| **OUT_PORT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-003 | HEX-003 | HEX-003 | HEX-003 |
| **IN_ADAPTER** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-004 | ok | ok |
| **OUT_ADAPTER** | ok | ok | ok | ok | HEX-004 | ok | ok | ok |
| **ROOT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |

### `layered`: Classic layered architecture

Presentation (INBOUND_ADAPTER) -> business (APPLICATION, ports, DOMAIN) -> persistence and integration (OUTBOUND_ADAPTER). Lower layers never depend on higher layers, and presentation does not bypass the business layer. Unlike hexagonal, the business layer may use persistence directly and the domain may depend on infrastructure APIs.

| from \ to | DOMAIN | APPLICATION | IN_PORT | OUT_PORT | IN_ADAPTER | OUT_ADAPTER | ROOT | infrastructure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **DOMAIN** | ok | LAYER-001 | LAYER-001 | ok | LAYER-001 | ok | LAYER-001 | ok |
| **APPLICATION** | ok | ok | ok | ok | LAYER-001 | ok | LAYER-001 | ok |
| **IN_PORT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | LAYER-001 | ok | LAYER-001 | ok |
| **OUT_PORT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | LAYER-001 | ok | LAYER-001 | ok |
| **IN_ADAPTER** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | LAYER-002 | ok | ok |
| **OUT_ADAPTER** | ok | LAYER-001 | LAYER-001 | ok | LAYER-001 | ok | LAYER-001 | ok |
| **ROOT** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |

### `modular-monolith`: Modular monolith

Each module is a declared bounded context with an explicit public API (exposedPackages). Modules may only use each other's public API, module dependencies must be acyclic, and package cycles are forbidden. Combine with hexagonal or layered for rules inside a module.

Includes: `ddd`.

Also activates: CYCLE-001.

## Rules

### CYCLE-001: Cycle among packages

Default severity ERROR; off unless enabled under `rules`; also activated by `clean`, `modular-monolith`.

Why: Package (Java), package/module (Python) or directory (TypeScript) cycles make code impossible to layer, split or understand in isolation. One finding is reported per strongly connected component.

Fix: Break at least one dependency in this component. Move a shared contract to an appropriate owner or invert a dependency through a port; verify that the full cycle is eliminated.

Java, violating:

```java
// com.acme.a.X uses com.acme.b.Y and com.acme.b.Y uses com.acme.a.Z
```

Java, compliant:

```java
// extract the shared type to com.acme.shared, or invert one edge through an interface
```

Python, violating:

```python
# pkg/a/x.py: from pkg.b import y ; pkg/b/y.py: from pkg.a import x
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# move the shared code into pkg/common and import it from both
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/a/x.ts imports ../b/y and src/b/y.ts imports ../a/x
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// move the shared type to src/shared and import it from both
```

### DDD-001: Cross-context access to a non-exposed package

Default severity ERROR; active with profile `ddd`, `modular-monolith`.

Why: Bounded contexts evolve independently only when other contexts depend on their published contract, not on their internals.

Fix: Use an explicitly exposed API or integration contract of {targetContext}. Keep its domain internals private to that context.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.billing.application;
import com.acme.orders.domain.Order;          // orders internals
```

Java, compliant:

```java
package com.acme.billing.application;
import com.acme.orders.api.OrderSummary;      // orders exposedPackages
```

Python, violating:

```python
# billing/application/invoice.py
from orders.domain.order import Order
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# billing/application/invoice.py
from orders.api import OrderSummary
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/billing/application/invoice.ts
import { Order } from "../../orders/domain/order";
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// src/billing/application/invoice.ts
import type { OrderSummary } from "../../orders/api";
```

### DDD-002: Cycle among bounded contexts

Default severity ERROR; active with profile `ddd`, `modular-monolith`.

Why: Mutually dependent contexts cannot be released, scaled or owned independently and usually indicate a misplaced concept.

Fix: Break at least one dependency in this component. Move a shared contract to an appropriate owner or invert a dependency through a port; verify that the full cycle is eliminated.

Java, violating:

```java
// orders uses billing.api.Invoice and billing uses orders.api.OrderSummary
```

Java, compliant:

```java
// billing depends on orders.api; orders publishes an OrderPlaced event instead of calling billing
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/application/x.py: from billing.api import Invoice
# billing/application/y.py: from orders.api import OrderSummary
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# orders publishes events consumed by billing; only billing imports orders.api
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/... imports src/billing/api and src/billing/... imports src/orders/api
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// only src/billing imports src/orders/api; orders emits domain events
```

### FW-001: HTTP endpoint outside an inbound adapter

Default severity ERROR; always active.

Why: Transport concerns (routing, status codes, serialization) belong to inbound adapters. Unclassified endpoints are not reported here; MODEL-001 can require their classification.

Fix: Move transport handling to an inbound adapter and delegate use-case execution through the application boundary.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.orders.application;
@RestController public class OrderService { @GetMapping("/orders") List<Order> all() {...} }
```

Java, compliant:

```java
package com.acme.orders.adapter.inbound.web;
@RestController class OrderController { private final ListOrders listOrders; }
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/application/service.py
@router.get("/orders")
def list_orders(): ...
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# orders/api/routes.py (INBOUND_ADAPTER)
@router.get("/orders")
def list_orders(use_case: ListOrders = Depends(...)): return use_case.run()
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/application/orders.service.ts
@Controller("orders") export class OrdersService { @Get() all() {} }
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// src/orders/api/orders.controller.ts (INBOUND_ADAPTER)
@Controller("orders") export class OrdersController { constructor(private listOrders: ListOrders) {} }
```

### FW-002: HTTP contract exposes a persistence entity

Default severity ERROR; always active.

Why: Returning or accepting persistence entities couples the public API to the storage schema, risks leaking fields and lazy-loading state, and blocks independent evolution of either side. Generic type arguments are included; nested DTO fields are not inspected recursively.

Fix: Introduce a transport DTO for this endpoint signature and map to/from the entity inside the adapter or application boundary. Update the documented API contract and its tests.

Java, violating:

```java
@GetMapping("/orders/{id}") public OrderEntity get(@PathVariable long id) { ... }
```

Java, compliant:

```java
@GetMapping("/orders/{id}") public OrderResponse get(@PathVariable long id) { ... }
```

Python, violating:

```python
@router.get("/orders/{id}")
def get(id: int) -> OrderModel: ...          # SQLAlchemy / Django model
```

Python, compliant:

```python
@router.get("/orders/{id}")
def get(id: int) -> OrderResponse: ...       # Pydantic DTO
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
@Get(":id") get(@Param("id") id: string): Promise<OrderEntity> { ... }   // TypeORM entity
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
@Get(":id") get(@Param("id") id: string): Promise<OrderResponseDto> { ... }
```

### HEX-001: Domain depends on an outer layer or framework

Default severity ERROR; active with profile `clean`, `hexagonal`.

Why: The domain model must be independent of use-case orchestration, adapters, wiring and infrastructure so it can be tested, reasoned about and reused without frameworks.

Fix: Remove this dependency from the domain. Move integration or orchestration outward; keep domain behavior in domain types and pass domain-oriented values.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.orders.domain;
import jakarta.persistence.Entity;          // infrastructure API in the domain
@Entity public class Order { }
```

Java, compliant:

```java
package com.acme.orders.domain;
public final class Order { /* pure domain state and behavior */ }
// JPA mapping lives in com.acme.orders.adapter.outbound.persistence.OrderEntity
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/domain/order.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped            # infrastructure in the domain
class Order(Base): id: Mapped[int]
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# orders/domain/order.py
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Order: id: int
# ORM model lives in orders/infra/persistence/models.py
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/domain/order.ts
import { Entity, Column } from "typeorm";    // infrastructure in the domain
@Entity() export class Order { @Column() id!: string; }
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// src/orders/domain/order.ts
export class Order { constructor(readonly id: string) {} }
// TypeORM entity lives in src/orders/infra/persistence/order.entity.ts
```

### HEX-002: Application depends on a concrete outer component

Default severity ERROR; active with profile `clean`, `hexagonal`.

Why: Use cases must depend on abstractions they own. Depending on a concrete adapter couples business flow to a specific technology and prevents substitution in tests.

Fix: Replace the concrete adapter dependency with an outbound port owned by the core. Implement the port in the adapter and wire it in the composition root.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.orders.application;
import com.acme.orders.adapter.outbound.SqlOrderStore;
public class PlaceOrder { private final SqlOrderStore store; }
```

Java, compliant:

```java
package com.acme.orders.application;
import com.acme.orders.port.outbound.OrderStore;   // core-owned port
public class PlaceOrder { private final OrderStore store; }
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/application/place_order.py
from orders.infra.sql_order_store import SqlOrderStore
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# orders/application/place_order.py
from orders.ports.order_store import OrderStore     # Protocol owned by the core
class PlaceOrder:
    def __init__(self, store: OrderStore): self.store = store
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/application/place-order.ts
import { SqlOrderStore } from "../infra/sql-order-store";
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// src/orders/application/place-order.ts
import type { OrderStore } from "../ports/order-store";   // interface owned by the core
export class PlaceOrder { constructor(private readonly store: OrderStore) {} }
```

### HEX-003: Port depends on an infrastructure or transport type

Default severity ERROR; active with profile `clean`, `hexagonal`.

Why: Ports are the core's contracts. Leaking adapter, framework or persistence types into them makes every caller and implementation depend on that technology.

Fix: Change the port contract to core-owned inputs and outputs. Map persistence, transport and vendor types inside the adapter.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.orders.port.outbound;
import org.springframework.data.domain.Page;
public interface OrderStore { Page<Order> findAll(); }
```

Java, compliant:

```java
package com.acme.orders.port.outbound;
public interface OrderStore { List<Order> findAll(int offset, int limit); }
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/ports/order_store.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
class OrderStore(Protocol):
    def find(self, session: Session, id: int): ...
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# orders/ports/order_store.py
class OrderStore(Protocol):
    def find(self, id: int) -> Order | None: ...
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/ports/order-store.ts
import type { Repository } from "typeorm";
export interface OrderStore { repo(): Repository<OrderEntity>; }
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// src/orders/ports/order-store.ts
import type { Order } from "../domain/order";
export interface OrderStore { find(id: string): Promise<Order | undefined>; }
```

### HEX-004: Inbound and outbound adapters depend directly on each other

Default severity ERROR; active with profile `clean`, `hexagonal`.

Why: A controller calling a repository directly bypasses use-case rules and transactions, and couples the transport contract to the storage model. Dependencies between adapters of the same direction are not covered; model those with constraints.

Fix: Route the operation through the application use case and its ports instead of coupling transport directly to persistence or another outbound adapter.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.orders.adapter.inbound.web;
import com.acme.orders.adapter.outbound.persistence.JpaOrderRepository;
@RestController class OrderController { JpaOrderRepository repo; }
```

Java, compliant:

```java
package com.acme.orders.adapter.inbound.web;
import com.acme.orders.port.inbound.PlaceOrderUseCase;
@RestController class OrderController { PlaceOrderUseCase placeOrder; }
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/api/routes.py
from orders.infra.repository import OrderRepository
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# orders/api/routes.py
from orders.application.place_order import PlaceOrder
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/api/order.controller.ts
import { OrderRepository } from "../infra/order.repository";
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// src/orders/api/order.controller.ts
import { PlaceOrder } from "../application/place-order";
```

### LAYER-001: Lower layer depends on a higher layer

Default severity ERROR; active with profile `layered`.

Why: In a layered architecture dependencies point downward only (presentation, then business, then persistence and integration). Upward dependencies create hidden cycles and block replacing a layer.

Fix: Invert the dependency: define the needed abstraction in the lower layer, or move the code into the layer that owns the behavior. Lower layers must never call presentation or wiring code.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.orders.persistence;
import com.acme.orders.service.OrderService;     // persistence -> business
```

Java, compliant:

```java
package com.acme.orders.service;
import com.acme.orders.persistence.OrderDao;     // business -> persistence
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/persistence/dao.py
from orders.service.order_service import OrderService
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# orders/service/order_service.py
from orders.persistence.dao import OrderDao
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/persistence/order.dao.ts
import { OrderService } from "../service/order.service";
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// src/orders/service/order.service.ts
import { OrderDao } from "../persistence/order.dao";
```

### LAYER-002: Presentation bypasses the business layer

Default severity ERROR; active with profile `layered`.

Why: Presentation code that talks to persistence directly skips business rules, validation and transaction boundaries.

Fix: Call an application service from the presentation layer and let it use persistence or integration code. Keep transport handlers free of data-access logic.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.orders.web;
import com.acme.orders.persistence.OrderDao;
```

Java, compliant:

```java
package com.acme.orders.web;
import com.acme.orders.service.OrderService;
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/web/views.py
from orders.persistence.dao import OrderDao
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# orders/web/views.py
from orders.service.order_service import OrderService
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/web/orders.controller.ts
import { OrderDao } from "../persistence/order.dao";
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// src/orders/web/orders.controller.ts
import { OrderService } from "../service/order.service";
```

### MODEL-001: Unit under roots has no declared role

Default severity ERROR; active when `requireClassification: true`.

Why: Boundary rules can only protect code whose role is known. Requiring classification prevents new code from silently escaping the architecture.

Fix: Map this package to a role in architecture.yml, or explicitly exclude it from analysis roots.

Java, violating:

```java
package com.acme.orders.util;   // matches roots, no role selector covers it
```

Java, compliant:

```java
# architecture.yml
roles:
  DOMAIN: ["com.acme.orders.domain..", "com.acme.orders.util.."]
```

Python, violating:

```python
# orders/helpers.py exists but no role selector covers orders.helpers
```

Python, compliant:

```python
roles:
  APPLICATION: ["orders.application.**", "orders.helpers"]
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
// src/orders/utils/x.ts exists but no role selector covers src/orders/utils
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
roles:
  DOMAIN: ["src/orders/domain/**", "src/orders/utils/**"]
```

### MODEL-002: Framework classification signals

Default severity INFO; always active.

Why: Framework annotations and base classes hint at a unit's intended role (endpoint, repository, entity). They are informational and never remap declared roles.

Fix: Review these signals when declaring roles. They do not prove active beans or runtime wiring.

Java, violating:

```java
@Repository class JpaOrders   // tag spring.repository; INFO only
```

Java, compliant:

```java
// map com.acme.orders.adapter.outbound.. to OUTBOUND_ADAPTER so the signal agrees with the role
```

Python, violating:

```python
class OrderModel(Base): ...   # tag persistence.entity; INFO only
```

Python, compliant:

```python
# map orders.infra.** to OUTBOUND_ADAPTER
```

Typescript, violating:

```ts
@Entity() export class OrderEntity {}   // tag persistence.entity; INFO only
```

Typescript, compliant:

```ts
// map src/orders/infra/** to OUTBOUND_ADAPTER
```
